gradient_duo.accuracy: O(h) on a quasi-uniform icosahedral triangular mesh
gradient_duo.reference: Heikes et al. (2023), J. Adv. Model. Earth Syst. 15:e2022MS003192 (DUO icosahedral triangular C-grid); the C-grid normal gradient, the discrete adjoint of divergence_duo. Maps a cell-centered scalar q to its edge-normal derivative: (grad q)_i = (q[faces_on_edge[i,2]] - q[faces_on_edge[i,1]]) / dv_edge[i], where i runs over EDGES (the edge-located output's index), faces_on_edge[i,1]=f_lo and faces_on_edge[i,2]=f_hi are the lower- and higher-indexed of edge i's two incident triangles, and dv_edge[i] is the great-circle distance between their circumcenters (the two cell centers). The result is the gradient component along the reference normal n̂_i (which points f_lo -> f_hi, matching edge_sign_on_face), so divergence_duo and gradient_duo share one orientation. Written as a reduction over the two incident faces s∈{1,2} with the centered-difference sign (2s-3) (s=1→-1 at f_lo, s=2→+1 at f_hi), exactly the implicit-output-index reduction form of divergence_duo but with the free index running over edges rather than cells. dv_edge and faces_on_edge are build-time-constant grid geometry; only q reaches the per-step hot tree.
